copies.headline: John's Bears Stack Buries Noah By 75
copies.body:
The Chicago half of John's roster decided this one before the afternoon window. Caleb Williams put up 37.3 and D'Andre Swift added 32.4, and with Trey McBride's 24.5 at tight end, John got 94.2 from three lineup spots — more than Noah's entire starting nine. The quarterback gap alone was 27.5, the running back gap 27.4, and the tight end gap 24.5, which is what happens when Colston Loveland posts a zero while Brenton Strange sits on the bench scoring 10.3.
Noah's receivers actually won their room by 14.7 and Rhamondre Stevenson's 14.5 beat John's flex by 7.5. None of it mattered. De'Von Achane missed his projection by 7.6, Drake Maye by 6.5, and the Titans defense contributed negative one point while the Patriots D/ST scored 7.0 in street clothes. John's own misses — Puka Nacua 8.7 short, Quentin Johnston 6.7 short — were rounding errors.
We had Noah by 9, which now reads like a dare. He's 0-11 in all-play, last in scoring. John is first in both, though the postseason assassin has been buried deeper than this in September.

copies.headline: Kaleb's Backs Bury Isaac's Broken Skill Corps
copies.body:
Running back decided this one before anything else did. Ashton Jeanty went for 32.7 and Breece Hall added 19.8, giving Kaleb 52.5 from the position against Isaac's 38.3 — and that 14.2 gap was the largest of the day. Ladd McConkey's 19.2 covered for Drake London (5.5 on a 13.8 projection) and Harold Fannin Jr. (4.1 on 11.1). Kaleb won five of seven positions and never needed to sweat the one he lost.
Isaac's problem was everything that wasn't a running back. Ja'Marr Chase scored 3.2 on a 19.9 projection, Bo Nix 5.4 on 16.1, Terry McLaurin 3.4 on 12.2. That's roughly 36 points of projection evaporating in one afternoon. Worse: Dalton Kincaid put up 18.0 on the bench, Malik Willis 16.7, Jakobi Meyers 12.2. Start any two and this is a different game.
We had Kaleb by 11; he doubled it. Isaac opens 0-1 with an all-play of 1-10 and the #12 power ranking, which means the loss wasn't bad luck — it was the roster.

copies.headline: Grant's Skill Positions Won, His Kicker Lost
copies.body:
Grant out-scored CJ 54.7 to 21.2 at receiver and 23.7 to 2.6 at tight end, which is normally the whole story. It wasn't. CJ won kicker by 8.8, D/ST by 11.0, FLEX by 18.1 and RB by 16.0, and that's the margin four times over. Harrison Mevis put up 1.0. The Steelers gave CJ 19.0 for free. Jonathan Taylor's 25.1 and Parker Washington's surprise 19.3 covered for Jake Ferguson's 2.6, which is a sentence nobody expected to write.
The killer was Jaylen Waddle: 1.2 on a 12.2 projection with Christian Watson putting up 32.7 on Grant's bench. Omarion Hampton (8.3 on 17.6) and Jadarian Price (7.8 on 14.1) didn't help. CJ left Chuba Hubbard's 23.7 rotting too, so nobody gets to feel clever here.
We had Grant by 11, which was wrong in the least interesting way possible. Grant's 116.3 was 7th in the league, CJ's 118.2 was 6th — a coin flip that landed on the owner with one winning season in four.

copies.headline: Adam's Backfield Buries Logan's Broken Backfield
copies.body:
The running backs settled this before anything else did. Kenneth Walker III went for 34.1 and Bucky Irving added 20.3, giving Adam 54.4 from the position against Logan's 22.0 — a 32.4-point hole in a game decided by 19.0. Logan actually won four of seven spots. Jalen Hurts outscored Jayden Daniels by 7.0, Isaiah Likely turned in a stunning 27.8 at tight end, and Justin Jefferson's 31.2 was the best single score on his side. None of it mattered, because Saquon Barkley managed 9.0 against a 17.7 projection and the Chargers defense produced a clean zero.
Adam won without his best available lineup, too. Jalen Coker put up 33.8 on the bench while Rome Odunze started and gave him 7.2 — a 26.6-point self-inflicted wound he never had to explain.
Adam is 1-0 with a 10-1 all-play, second in scoring, and the top spot in the power rankings. Logan is 0-1 despite finishing third in points, which is the exact brand of luck the man who wore the dress last year did not need in September. We picked Logan by 11. We were not close.

copies.headline: Peter's Kicker Outscores Half His Receivers
copies.body:
The kicker won this. Evan McPherson's 19.5 was worth more to Peter than A.J. Brown and George Pickens combined, and it covered the 17.5-point hole Brandon Aubrey's two-point dud dug for Christian. Everywhere else Christian had the edge that mattered: plus-9.2 at receiver, plus-13 on defense with Seattle, plus-4 in the flex. He lost by 1.4 because his kicker hit one field goal and Peter's hit everything.
Not that Peter earned it cleanly. Brown and Pickens missed projection by a combined 17.5 while Kyle Monangai put up 20.4 in street clothes on his bench. Bijan Robinson's 31.3 carried the whole thing. On the other side, George Kittle's 3.2 and DeVonta Smith's 8.3 sank Christian, and Deebo Samuel's 18.0 sat next to Smith the entire afternoon.
We picked Christian by nine, which was correct about everything except the kickers. The all-play says both of these teams should be 0-1; Peter is 1-0 on 0.7 wins of luck, which is a fine place for a Lundquist to start.

copies.headline: Leif's Running Backs Outrun A Dead Tight End
copies.body:
Leif won this on the ground and nowhere else. Derrick Henry 35.3, David Montgomery 28.9 out of the flex, Christian McCaffrey chipping in 13.8 — that's a +10.8 edge at running back and a +25.8 edge at flex, and he needed every bit of it, because his wide receivers gave him 9.9 combined and Kyle Pitts Sr. gave him a clean zero. Josh Allen's 35.7 covered the rest. Margin: 1.7.
Mitchell actually won the passing game 42.2 to 9.9 at receiver and won tight end by 10.3, which tells you where this went wrong. Courtland Sutton 3.1 on an 11.7 projection while Matthew Golden put up 15.5 on the bench is the whole loss. Rachaad White's 4.7 didn't help. Jaxson Dart and Jahmyr Gibbs did their jobs.
We picked Leif by nine and he cleared by two, which counts. Mitchell is 0-1 with the fifth-best scoring in the league and a luck rating of -0.6 — the human coin flip landing on edge, as usual.

intro: Three games decided by under two points — Peter over Christian by 1.4, Leif over Mitchell by 1.66, CJ over Grant by 1.82 — which means half this league spent Monday night doing math on a kicker. At the other end, John hung 159.46 on Noah's 84.22, the kind of gap where the second half is less a comeback attempt than a hostage situation. Adam's 156.26 was the only other score north of 140, and it still cost Logan a very respectable 137.
